title: Proposal for Shorter COE Renewal Durations As A More Affordable Option
what_it_is: Proposal for Shorter COE Renewal Durations As A More Affordable Option

sections.label: Five-year COE renewal concession
sections.summary: Existing car owners may renew COEs for five years, and shorter renewals would amplify COE cycles and cut new COE supply.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Today, we already allow existing car owners to renew COEs for five years as a concession.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: If we allow for shorter renewals, this is likely to amplify the peak and the trough of the COE cycles further.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: It would mean that more car owners could renew their COEs when prices are high and this would reduce the supply of new COEs for prospective car owners.

sections.label: Commercial vehicle COE renewals
sections.summary: Commercial vehicle owners may renew COEs for five years up to statutory vehicle life, and businesses should bid in the same market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: I fully understand the concerns of small business owners who need to continue to have their vehicles to operate, especially in the environment of high COE prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We already similarly allow commercial vehicle owners to renew their COEs for five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: And in fact, they can do it until the statutory life of their vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: It is something that I think is fair, because you also want to allow for new businesses who wish to have access to vehicles to be able to compete for COEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: I think the better approach is for them to be able to bid in the same market and therefore, for the COE to be priced accordingly.
